lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 21: troubleshooting Pods
lesson.description: Break six Pods on purpose and fix each one: Pending, ImagePullBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError, RunContainerError, CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled.
lesson.tested: Six broken Pods created, read and fixed on kind v0.33.0, node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Read the STATUS, then the one place it points to: Events for scheduling and pulls, Last State for config, start and memory failures, logs for the app. The fix is almost always in the message.

cheatsheet.intro: Six STATUS values, and the commands from Lesson 21.

rows.name: Pending
rows.role: Not scheduled, or not started. The lab's pending Pod asked for 64 CPU. The event said Insufficient cpu.

rows.name: ImagePullBackOff
rows.role: ErrImagePull is the failed pull. ImagePullBackOff is the wait. The lab's tag ended in not found.

rows.name: Config error
rows.role: CreateContainerConfigError. The container was not created. The lab was a missing ConfigMap app-config.

rows.name: RunContainerError
rows.role: The command could not start. Last State was StartError, exit 128. There are no app logs.

rows.name: CrashLoopBackOff
rows.role: The app started and exited. The kubelet waits 10s, then 20, 40, up to 300s. The cause is in the logs.

rows.name: OOMKilled
rows.role: The container was killed for memory. Exit code 137. The lab set a 32Mi limit.

boards.title: Fixes the lab used
boards.hint: most of them need a new Pod

rows.name: pending
rows.role: Lower the CPU request. The lesson used replace --force so the Pod is deleted and created again.

rows.name: typo
rows.role: The image was nginx:1.29-alpnie. set image can change a Pod image in place.

rows.name: config
rows.role: Create the ConfigMap. The Pod started and the logs said mode=prod. No replace.

rows.name: oom
rows.role: Left broken on purpose. Raise the limit or fix the leak. Exit 137.

items.what: Pending, image pull and missing config happen before the process runs. Only a crash leaves the app's own error in the logs.
The delay doubles from 10 seconds up to five minutes, and it resets after a container has run for 10 minutes.
logs --previous failed while crash still showed Error, because the older container was already gone. After the container stayed up between crashes, --previous worked.
Running and 1/1 mean the container runs and its readiness probe passes. A request that fails on the way in is a Service problem, covered in part 22.

commands.cmd: kubectl set image pod/typo web=nginx:1.29-alpine -n k8s-from-zero
commands.note: an image can change in place

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace k8s-from-zero. The lesson's six Pods are pending, typo, config, runerr, crash and oom. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: Which three failures happen before the app runs, and which three after?
exercises.a: Before: Pending, image pulls, and missing config. After: start errors, crashes, and OOM kills. Only a crash leaves the app's own error in the logs.

exercises.q: What is the difference between ErrImagePull and ImagePullBackOff?
exercises.a: ErrImagePull is the failed attempt. ImagePullBackOff is the wait before the next one. The delay grows and is capped at 300 seconds. not found means the registry answered and the tag does not exist.

exercises.q: Why does OOMKilled show exit code 137?
exercises.a: The kubelet killed the container for memory. The lab's container had a 32Mi limit and wrote until it was killed. Raise the limit or fix the leak.

exercises.q: Describe the pending Pod. What FailedScheduling message did the lesson record?
exercises.a: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. The Pod requested 64 CPU. Preemption was not helpful. Lowering the request and replacing the Pod made it Running.

exercises.q: Describe config before the ConfigMap exists. What reason do you see, and what starts the Pod?
exercises.a: CreateContainerConfigError. The event names the missing ConfigMap. kubectl create configmap app-config with mode=prod lets the Pod start, and the logs say mode=prod.

exercises.q: Describe runerr and read Last State. What reason, exit code and message shape did the lesson record?
exercises.a: RunContainerError, Last State StartError, exit 128. The message names the missing file. There are no application logs, because the process never started.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: logs --previous fails while the Pod still shows Error. What did the lesson observe?
exercises.a: The previous container was already gone, so there were no logs to read. After the container stayed running between crashes, --previous returned the earlier output.

exercises.q: All six Pods look fine in get pods, and the app still fails requests. Where does the lesson send you?
exercises.a: Running and 1/1 only mean the container runs and its readiness probe passes. Failures on the way in are a Service or routing problem. Part 22 covers them.

exercises.q: You fix a field that set image cannot change. What does the lesson say to do?
exercises.a: Fix the manifest, or the Deployment that owns the Pod, and replace the Pod. Most fields need a new Pod. kubectl replace --force -f FILE deletes and creates it.
